headline: Highest risk is medium: Plandex can write/execute shell in a shared plan-local sandbox, while python-cheatsheet is read-only documentation, so prompt-injection and data-leakage paths are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex can read/write a project directory and uses a review-then-apply sandbox, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-runnable. The pair lacks a direct automated channel, so injection mainly requires manual copy/paste or shared files, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator copies python-cheatsheet text into Plandex prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF both are pointed at the same writable project directory, file-based prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet content out of Plandex prompts unless quoted verbatim for review.
Use separate directories for the two agents.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex during review.
Manually inspect any file content before Plandex consumes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex can read the filesystem and has broad network egress, but python-cheatsheet touches no files, APIs, or secrets. There is no documented shared workspace or credential overlap, so leakage is limited to accidental exposure of local code if the operator places it in Plandex's project directory.
conditions: IF source code or secrets are placed in Plandex's project directory, Plandex can read them.
IF the operator exports Plandex outputs into a shared repo or paste buffer, content can leak to downstream systems.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the Plandex workspace.
Use a throwaway repo for experiments.
Review Plandex outputs before sharing them externally.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state is via the Plandex server backend. python-cheatsheet is non-runnable, so it does not create write contention itself; however, the shared backend plus Plandex's write/git abilities create a real conflict path in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF two Plandex instances operate on the same backend-backed plan, write conflicts can occur.
IF the operator enables concurrent edits to the same git worktree, state races become possible.
mitigations: Run only one Plandex instance per worktree.
Avoid concurrent git edits during a plan.
Use separate branches for parallel work.
Pause one instance before applying changes from another.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses review-then-apply, which reduces blind trust in upstream text, and python-cheatsheet is only a reference document. The pair can still cascade if the operator pastes cheat-sheet-derived text into Plandex and then applies changes without review, but that is not the default path.
conditions: IF the operator treats python-cheatsheet snippets as authoritative instructions inside Plandex, errors can propagate.
IF auto-apply is enabled and review is skipped, incorrect edits can cascade into the repo.
mitigations: Cross-check any code advice against a second source.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is identified for either agent: Plandex touches source code and model-provider keys, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data. There is no evidence of residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch in the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into Plandex, a separate compliance review is required.
IF the operator stores secrets in the project directory, local policy may be implicated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager.
Review retention settings before using Plandex on sensitive repos.
